items.title: Nicki Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe. Utica, New York, November 6, 2010 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: So I did that for a while and then on Thursday and Friday I did lunchtimes with George Coleman Junior on drums and Gloria Coleman on piano, at the Film Center in New York.

ctx.x: And so no, I didn’t know if I was going to — I really left Australia saying I’m just going for the summer, the New York summer, the American summer, I’m just going for a few months, I’ll see you maybe in October or November. Very vague. It totally scared the life out of my parents. You know I was 24, and just brave I guess. Crazy or brave, I don’t know which one. But I rose to the challenge. Soon after I met this Australian girl and I worked in fashion for eight months. Because I really didn’t know if I was ever…

is a wonderful piano player. I think it paid like 30 bucks or something like that. It was like a lunchtime gig at the Film Center. So I did Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday I worked in fashion selling prints to fashion designers. And that world was crazy. That was a crazy world. The whole fashion world. Skinny girls and gay guys pretty much. So I thought well, this is something different. You know, very competitive and but interesting kind of, it was creative. And so I did that for eight months. And I sold all these…
